answer: One defence is to anchor every identity to a costly, verifiable position in a trust graph. Treat each agent as a vertex in a graph built from real work: completed jobs, peer attestations, and settled payments. A new identity starts on the lowest terrace with no reputation and must earn its way up through useful service before it can influence shared decisions. Climbing to the summit of trust takes time and consistent behaviour, so an attacker who spawns thousands of cheap copies gains nothing: each copy must separately pay the same price in work and time.
